component.name: LibreDB Studio
component.summary: AI-powered SQL IDE for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and more

description.p: LibreDB Studio is an open-source SQL IDE for developers and data teams. The desktop app runs entirely on your machine: it starts a local LibreDB Studio server in the background and shows it in a native window. It reaches the databases you configure and, if you turn the optional AI features on, the model provider you pick. Nothing else leaves the machine.

ul.li: IBM Db2 for Linux, UNIX and Windows
Milvus (read-only, with admin Load and Release)
A Monaco-based SQL editor with schema-aware completion and formatting
A virtualized results grid built for large result sets, with CSV and JSON export
Schema browser, entity-relationship diagrams and index advice
Query plans, slow-query and session monitoring
Optional AI query explanation on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, libSQL, DuckDB, Couchbase, ClickHouse, Apache Druid and Trino, through Gemini, OpenAI, a local Ollama or your own endpoint
An embedded sample database, so there is something to query on first launch

description.p: Connections are made over TCP. The sandbox has no access to your home directory by default; grant it explicitly if you need to open SQLite or DuckDB files or reach a database through a Unix socket - the project documentation lists the exact commands.

screenshot.caption: Running a query and browsing results in the SQL editor

description.p: A JWT signing secret shorter than 32 characters now stops the app at startup with an explanatory message, instead of starting up and failing every login.

Every download for this release is now cryptographically attested, and the npx launcher verifies that attestation before it starts the app. The SQL editor also serves its own Monaco assets, so the workspace opens on a machine with no internet access.

The desktop build now also ships a GUI Debian package alongside the AppImage, and the bundled Node runtime is installed as libredb-studio-node so it cannot claim a path the distribution's nodejs package owns.
Auth cookies can now drop the Secure flag on a deployment the browser reaches over plain HTTP, so a login holds on a trusted local network.
First release with the desktop application: the AppImage this Flatpak repacks.
